hero.title: Track what you watch, on your own server.
hero.body: rwnd.tv is an open source, self-hosted app for tracking the TV shows and films you watch — a replacement for trakt.tv that you run yourself. Log by hand, import your Trakt history, or let Plex log it for you.
hero.meta: MIT licensed · Docker image on GHCR · Node 22 + PostgreSQL · Light, dark and system themes

m2.label: M2 · done
m2.body: Trakt import, galleries, Plex webhooks, export

m3.label: M3 · in progress
m3.body: Ratings and watchlists shipped; first tagged release next

honest.label: Honestly:
honest.body: no tagged release yet, and the security review is still open.

features.title: What works today
features.body: Everything listed here is shipped and running on the live instance. Nothing below is a plan.

log.title: Search and log
log.body: Find a film or a specific episode, log that you watched it, and browse your History — every watch, rating, watchlist add and drop in one place.

plex.title: Plex logs it for you
plex.body: Point Plex at your webhook URL and watches log themselves. Multi-user servers are first class: every Plex account seen is claimed to its own rwnd.tv user, and earlier watches are backfilled on claim.

trakt.title: Bring your Trakt data
trakt.body: Import history, ratings and watchlist — either over OAuth or from the ZIP that Trakt's own "Export now" gives you, so the one-connected-app cap isn't in your way.

galleries.title: Poster galleries
galleries.body: TV Shows and Films each get a poster wall, with per-show watch progress, genre include/exclude and release-year filters, and twelve sort orders.

lists.title: Watchlists and ratings
lists.body: Any number of named lists plus a one-click default, and a 5-star rating for shows, films and individual episodes — independent of whether you've watched them.

export.title: Your data stays yours
export.body: A CSV per category — history, ratings, watchlist, dropped shows — zipped and downloadable from Settings. Open formats, no lock-in, by design.

selfHost.title: Three steps to running it
selfHost.body: A Docker image and a compose file. You bring a PostgreSQL database and a TMDB or TheTVDB API key.
selfHost.docsPrompt: Configuration reference, backup and upgrade notes:
selfHost.registrationNote: Registration on your instance can be open, invite-only or closed.

run.title: Run it
run.body: Pull the compose file, fill in .env, and bring it up on the box you already have.

import.title: Bring your history
import.body: Import from Trakt over OAuth, upload Trakt's ZIP export, or load a CSV.

current.title: Keep it current
current.body: Add the Plex webhook and your per-user API token, or keep logging by hand.

gallery.title: A look at the app
gallery.body: Plain, fast, keyboard-friendly, and themed light or dark to match your system.

status.title: Where the project actually is
status.body: Two milestones are done and the third is under way. The roadmap in the repo is a living document and this page follows it rather than getting ahead of it.

m1.title: M1 — Foundation
items: Local accounts, sessions, per-user API tokens
TMDB search, manual watch logging, history
Docker image, CI and a GHCR release pipeline

status.builtTitle: Built with Claude Code, in the open.
status.builtBody: The author isn't a web developer, and has said so from day one — the vision doc, the ADRs and the roadmap are all in the repo, and so is the reasoning behind every significant choice.

selfHost.q: Do I have to self-host it?
selfHost.aOpen: No. rwnd.tv runs a public instance you can sign up for, and the same Docker image serves it. Every instance decides its own registration policy: open, invite-only or closed.
selfHost.aClosed: No. rwnd.tv runs a public instance, though it isn't taking new sign-ups right now — the same Docker image serves it, so self-hosting is the way in for now. Every instance decides its own registration policy: open, invite-only or closed.

dropIn.q: Is it a drop-in Trakt replacement yet?
dropIn.a: Not entirely. Import, logging, galleries, watchlists, ratings and Plex scrobbling all work. Stats and insights, an upcoming-episodes calendar, and shareable profiles aren't scheduled yet.

metadata.q: Where does the metadata come from?
metadata.a: TMDB and TheTVDB, both behind a provider interface rather than called directly — so a more open source can join or replace them later without a rewrite.

requirements.q: What do I need to run it?
requirements.a: Docker, a PostgreSQL database and a TMDB or TheTVDB API key. To work on it: Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm.

players.a: Not yet. Plex shipped first, but the ingestion core is source-agnostic on purpose — each additional player is one payload parser and one route, not a rework.

1.label: Avoid
1.meaning: Beyond saving. Not worth the time.

2.label: Flawed
2.meaning: Noticeable problems. Really only for devotees of the series, genre or cast.

3.label: Worth watching
3.meaning: Genuinely has merit. Time well spent if the genre or series appeals to you.

4.label: Highly recommended
4.meaning: Well made and enjoyable — comfortable to recommend to almost anyone.

5.label: Essential
5.meaning: Among the best you'll see. Drop everything and watch it.
